function.name: get_air_quality
function.description: Retrieve real-time air quality and pollution data for a specific location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city that you want to get the air quality data for.

detail.description: If true, additional data like PM2.5, PM10, ozone levels, and pollution sources will be retrieved. the value is set to false to default.

historical.description: Optional date (in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format) to retrieve historical data.

message.reasoning: The user wants real-time air quality data for New York City, including today, yesterday, and day before yesterday, with additional data like PM2.5, PM10, ozone levels, and pollution sources. They mention today is 2023-05-05. We need to call the function get_air_quality. The location is "New York City". We need detail true. For historical we need to provide dates for yesterday and day before yesterday. But the function signature only allows one historical date? It says optional date to retrieve historical data. So maybe we can call multiple times? The user wants data for today, yesterday, and day before yesterday. We can call get_air_quality three times: once for today (historical="2023-05-05"), once for yesterday (historical="2023-05-04"), once for day before yesterday (historical="2023-05-03"). Or we can call once for today with detail true and historical default "today" (which is 2023-05-05). Then call twice more for historical dates. The function returns any. We'll call it three times.
